country.evidence_source: [page/5/Text/17] This finding is consistent with the study conducted on a representative Chinese sample (Bai et al., 2011), which also found that item 4 (along with item 5) was noninvariant across age. A recent cross-national study among the adults in the US, England, and Japan (Whisman & Judd, 2016) found that intercepts of item 4 were noninvariant across three countries, suggesting that this item may evoke different interpretations across cultures. In sum, the evidence of noninvariance for item 4 obtained in numerous studies raises the question of whether this item could be removed from the SWLS. This issue warrants further clarification and future research is needed to investigate whether the SWLS is able to measures life satisfaction adequately if this item is dropped from the scale. [page/5/Text/18] The latent mean comparisons on the SWLS revealed significant differences across age and gender. The results showed that adolescents reported higher life satisfaction than students and adults, with adults showing the lowest life satisfaction. This decline in life satisfaction with age in Serbia is in accordance with the results of previous studies conducted in poorer countries.
